prompt:
Write a police officer's crash report narrative (about 150 words). Collision type: rear-end collision in Sugar Land, Texas. The claimant was a driver and reported whiplash. Refer to people as Driver 1, Driver 2 or Passenger. No names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1106; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Witnesses, photos and the other driver all confirm the accident happened as described.
- The damage is mostly in line with the described impact.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text: Driver 1 was stopped in the right lane of southbound traffic on a Sugar Land roadway when the rear of their vehicle was struck by Driver 2's vehicle, which had been following too closely. Driver 1 reported neck pain and stiffness consistent with whiplash and was assisted from the scene by medics. The Passenger, seated in the front right seat, was also present in the vehicle at the time of impact and confirmed the sequence of events. Driver 2 acknowledged the collision and stated that they had been distracted briefly before braking. Two independent witnesses in a nearby vehicle observed the impact and described it the same way the drivers did. Photographs taken at the scene show rear-end damage to Driver 1's vehicle, with the extent of the damage generally matching the reported speed and force of the impact. Officers found no sign of prior damage to either vehicle. Driver 1 was identified as a named insured on the policy covering the vehicle. Both vehicles were driven from the scene after the report was completed.
